_comment: Labelled evaluation set: the ground truth of the Judge harness.
No rule passage appears here, deliberately. The harness replays OrchestratorService.resolve(),
so rules always come from the real RuleRetriever; a case forging its own passages would never
get a citation attested, and would measure the fixture instead of the system.
Dates are relative, never absolute: a deadline rule once expired three absolute fixtures at once
without a single assertion turning red.
'deterministic': a Java rule settles it (amount, deadline), so EvalCorpusTest replays it with no key.
Six of the eleven catalogue reason codes are exercised. The other five are out of scope because
the mocked data cannot ground them, and the missing field is named: 11.3 / 4808 (no authorisation
field), 12.6 (no way to represent a duplicate), 13.2 (no recurring-subscription field), 4834 (no
point-of-interaction error field). Including them would mean inventing their ground truth, and
reasonCodeAccuracy would then measure the consistency of my own labels rather than the system.
Three labels were corrected after the first run (EVAL-009, 010, 012), and the reason matters:
that run scored decisionAccuracy 0.55, and six of the nine failures came from a contradiction
between two documents I had written myself - the prompt ordered 'insufficient evidence ->
ESCALATE' while the corpus expected ACCEPT on empty files, and the model obeyed the prompt.
The prompt gave way on three of them (v1.2.0). On the other three my label was simply wrong:
a delivery record answers neither 'not as described' nor 'quality disputed', and 'shipped' is
not 'delivered'. The three genuine model errors (EVAL-001, 007, 011) were NOT touched: an eval
whose failures get relabelled measures nothing.

cases.issuerClaim: Cardholder states they did not authorise this online purchase.
cases.why: 3DS failed, AVS MISMATCH, IP inconsistent with billing: no liability shift, representment is lost before it starts.

cases.issuerClaim: Cardholder does not recognise this transaction on their statement.
cases.why: 3DS AUTHENTICATED: liability shifts to the issuer. Green signals and a loyal customer.

cases.issuerClaim: Cardholder reports the merchandise was never received.
cases.why: Complete delivery record (shipped, tracking, DELIVERED): the decisive argument against a not-received reason code.

cases.issuerClaim: Cardholder states the item does not match the description on the website.
cases.why: 1,500.00 EUR over the 1,000 EUR threshold. The amount rule wins over an otherwise strong file (ADR-0012).

cases.issuerClaim: Cardholder denies authorising this transaction.
cases.why: First Mastercard case in the project. 3DS AUTHENTICATED, customer with history on the same card.

cases.issuerClaim: Cardholder states the goods were never provided.
cases.why: Physical goods with no fulfilment record at all: the merchant has nothing to answer with. Exact mirror of EVAL-003.

cases.issuerClaim: Cardholder reports a fraudulent charge they did not make.
cases.why: 3DS only ATTEMPTED, AVS and CVV both MISMATCH, IP outside the billing country: indefensible.

cases.issuerClaim: Cardholder claims this charge was not authorised by them.
cases.why: Second path to REPRESENT on 10.4: 3DS authenticated and an earlier purchase on the same card.

cases.issuerClaim: Cardholder reports the parcel never arrived.
cases.why: SHIPPED is not DELIVERED: status IN_TRANSIT. Evidence exists but does not settle the claim. Label corrected after the first run - it said ACCEPT, conflating 'no evidence' with 'inconclusive evidence'.

cases.issuerClaim: Cardholder states the delivered item is not as described.
cases.why: A delivery record establishes RECEIPT and says nothing about CONFORMITY: it does not answer the reason code raised. Label corrected after the first run - it said REPRESENT, crediting the merchant with off-topic evidence.

cases.issuerClaim: Cardholder denies making this purchase.
cases.why: Weak counterpart of 4837: 3DS NOT_AUTHENTICATED, AVS MISMATCH, foreign IP. Checks the MC path is not wired to a single verdict.

cases.issuerClaim: Cardholder disputes the quality of the goods received.
cases.why: Same flaw as EVAL-010 on the Mastercard path: delivery does not answer a QUALITY dispute. Label corrected after the first run.

cases.issuerClaim: Cardholder is dissatisfied with the goods and reports the merchant did not resolve it.
cases.why: No fulfilment leg, AVS and CVV unverified, 3DS only attempted: nothing to answer with.

cases.issuerClaim: Cardholder states the goods were not provided by the merchant.
cases.why: Strong counterpart of 4855 facing EVAL-006: same reason code, complete delivery record.

cases.issuerClaim: Cardholder reports the merchandise was never received.
cases.why: Deadline expired five days ago. The file is excellent - same transaction as EVAL-003, which yields REPRESENT: the calendar decides, not the facts (ADR-0015).

cases.issuerClaim: Cardholder denies authorising this transaction.
cases.why: Due in two days, under the three calendar-day margin: no time left to build the case.

cases.issuerClaim: Cardholder denies authorising this high-value purchase.
cases.why: 2,500.00 EUR. Amount rule on the Visa path.

cases.issuerClaim: Cardholder denies authorising this transaction.
cases.why: Unknown transaction: empty bundle, the orchestrator escalates without calling the decision engine. Not deterministic despite appearances - the evidence agent does call the model before returning an empty bundle.

cases.issuerClaim: Cardholder denies authorising this transaction.
cases.why: 1,800.00 EUR. The same amount rule on the Mastercard path: a rule exercised on one network only is half checked.

cases.issuerClaim: Cardholder states the goods were never provided.
cases.why: The exact boundary: 100000 minor units, the threshold itself. The rule says strictly greater, so no escalation - the model decides, and on a file with no delivery evidence it must accept.
